subject: Two different categories in one scatterplot

messages.author: f5bec70b36df06aa
messages.subject: Two different categories in one scatterplot
parts:
Hi @all

I have a dataset with surface water and groundwater samples for two
different catchments. The code I am using produces a scatterplot
matrix showing the different water types in two different shapes
(round for surface and triangle for groundwater) and the two
catchments where they are sampled from in two different colours (red
for catchment 1 and blue for catchment 2). However, I don't want to
use colours and I couldn't figure out how to use fill or no-fill
instead of colours for the two different catchments. Any help would be
greatly appreciated.

Here is the code I am using:

read.csv("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/4236038/dotplots_all.csv") ->
nutrients
p<-ggplot(nutrients, aes(x = d18O, y = dD, shape=factor(Water)))
p+geom_point()
p<-ggplot(nutrients, aes(x = d18O, y = dD, shape=factor(Water),
color=factor(Catchment)))
p+geom_point(size=4)+ geom_abline(intercept = 10.8, slope = 8.13)
+geom_abline(intercept = 12.56, slope = 7.72, linetype="dashed")+
theme_bw() + opts(legend.key=theme_rect(fill=NULL,colour=NULL)) +
opts(legend.position = "bottom") +
xlab(expression(paste(delta^{18},'O'~'(\u2030)'))) +
ylab(expression(paste(delta,'D'~'(\u2030)'))) + opts(axis.text.x =
theme_text(size=13), axis.text.y = theme_text(size=13, hjust = 0.8),
legend.title = theme_text(size=15), legend.text = theme_text(size=15),
axis.title.x = theme_text(size=15), axis.title.y = theme_text(size=15,
angle = 90)) + opts(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.4))+
opts(legend.background=theme_rect(col = "black")) + opts(panel.border
= theme_rect(colour = 'black')) + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-5,2)) +
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-20,15))

Thanks,
Martin

messages.author: 07fb939f5d771778
messages.subject: Re: Two different categories in one scatterplot
parts:
hi you need to make a new column in your csv (name it eg labeltype)
presumably there will be 4 possibilities (round/triangle, filled/
unfilled) : open triangle=24, closed triangle=16 etc

whether you do this by hand or with some sort of logical expression in
excel or R is obviously another story...

then use shape=factor(labeltype) and probably drop the
color=(Catchment)

HTH
ben
ps. i am a ggplot novice too but i did something similar already

Thanks for the idea.

I tried that already but I guess my brain was not working properly
because I didn't know how to use this new column. But now it works
like a charme. I did:

nutrients$col<-paste(nutrients$Water, nutrients$Catchment) #merge by
paste
p<-ggplot(nutrients, aes(x = d18O, y = dD, shape=factor(col)))
p+geom_point()
